text_blocks.snippet: ARV prophylaxis refers to the use of antiretroviral (ARV) drugs to prevent HIV infection. It can be categorized into pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for those at high risk of HIV acquisition and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for those who have been potentially exposed to HIV.
snippet_highlighted_words: the use of antiretroviral (ARV) drugs to prevent HIV infection

text_blocks.snippet: PrEP is for HIV-negative individuals who are at substantial risk of HIV infection. It involves taking ARV medications (pills or injections) regularly to significantly reduce the risk of HIV acquisition if exposed. PrEP can be an option for individuals who may be exposed to HIV through sexual activity or injection drug use.

PEP is an emergency measure that involves taking ARV drugs within 72 hours of a potential HIV exposure to prevent infection. It's typically used after a potential exposure through sexual activity, sharing needles, or other routes.
